findings.desc: doc-code-drift: §2.2 FINDING schema declares severity as BLOCKER|MAJOR|MINOR, but §4.2 flow feeds confirmed Findings into finding_add, which only accepts severity critical|high|medium|low (cli/command-catalog.ts:1451, core/types.ts:532 Finding interface). BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR are not valid Lattice Finding severity values and would cause a Zod validation error at finding_add call time. The spec schema should either (a) use the actual Lattice severity enum critical|high|medium|low, or (b) explicitly state this is a methodological label layer that maps to Lattice severity before finding_add is called.

doc-code-drift: §2.3 Verdict schema declares agreedSeverity as BLOCKER|MAJOR|MINOR|NOT_A_DEFECT. This is the same severity-label mismatch as §2.2: Lattice finding_add uses critical|high|medium|low, not BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR. Additionally, NOT_A_DEFECT is introduced in §2.3 without being part of the Finding severity enum. If Verdict.agreedSeverity is ever stored or mapped to a finding_add call, the BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR values cannot be passed directly. The spec needs to either use the Lattice severity vocabulary or explicitly define the translation layer between its methodological labels and Lattice severity values.

Codex MAJOR (lane list wrong): the spec names lattice-review-scope/test/delivery as REVIEW lanes, but review_run_start supports concept/quality/test-coverage/behavior/docs/channel; scope-plan + delivery are PLAN/DONE artifacts not review_run lanes. Fix §4.1/§5: use the actual supported REVIEW lanes, map each lens to one, describe scope-plan/delivery as separate PLAN/DONE artifacts (or mark a new completeness lane as FUTURE).
